Irit Aviram, Ph. D., Professor of Biochemistry
Born: 16/5/1937 Krakow, Poland
Education:
1957-1963 Tel-Aviv University Microbiology M.Sc. 1963
1965-1969 Tel-Aviv University Biochemistry Ph.D. 1970
Professional experience
1970-1974 Lecturer, Dept. Biochemistry, Tel-Aviv University
1971 Visiting Scientist (EMBO Fellow) E.T.H. Zurich
1974-1983 Senior Lecturer, Dept. Biochemistry, Tel-Aviv University
1976 Visiting Scientist, Dept. Physiology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York
1981 Visiting Scientist (EMBO Fellow) Physical Chemistry, Lund University, Sweden
1982 Det. Hematology and Oncology, Tufts University, New England Medical Center Hospital, Boston
1983-1990 Assoc.Professor, Dept. Biochemistry, Tel-Aviv University
1988 Biochemistry, Scripps Clinics and Research Foundation, La Jolla, CA
1990 Dept. Biochemistry, Tel-Aviv University

PUBLICATIONS.

I. Aviram, Y.P. Meyer and A. Schejter (1981): Stepwise modification of electrostatic charge of cytochrome c. J. Biol. Chem. 256: 5540 - 5544.

I. Aviram (1981): The interaction of benzhydroxamic acid with horeseradish peroxidase and its fluorescent analogs.
Arch. Biochem. Biophys. 212: 483-490.

I. Aviram and N. Shaklai (1981): The association of human erythrocyte catalase with cell membrane. Arch. Biochem. Biophys. 212: 329-337.
A. Schejter, I. Aviram and T. Goldkorn (1982) The Contribution of electrostatic factors to the oxidation-reduction potentials of C-type cytochromes. In: Electron Transport and Oxygen Utilization, (Chien Ho, ed.), pp. 96 - 99, MacMillan Press.

L. Sasson, M. Sharabani and I. Aviram.(1982) The oxidation of anilinonaphtalene dyes by horseradish peroxidase. Arch Biochem. Biophys. 217: 529-535.

A. Aviram and I. Aviram (1983): Activation of the respiratory burst in guinea pig neutrophils by DCCD. FEBS Letters 155: 205-208
